annotatedSteps.description: Stating tetravalency and sharing of valence electrons to form covalent bonds
annotatedSteps.studentWork: Carbon ke paas 4 valence electrons hain. ... isliye electrons share karta hai — so it forms covalent bonds.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ½ Mentioned 4 valence electrons and sharing, but use standard English/Hindi scientific terminology (noble gas configuration/octet).
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking: Carbon has 4 valence electrons. To attain a stable noble gas configuration, it shares these valence electrons with other atoms, forming covalent bonds.

annotatedSteps.description: Explaining the scientific reasons why carbon cannot form C4- or C4+ ions
annotatedSteps.studentWork: Woh 4 electrons na gain kar sakta hai na lose karna easy hai
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Reason not explained: state that 6 protons cannot hold 10 electrons (C4-), and removing 4 electrons requires a huge amount of energy (C4+).
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking: It cannot gain 4 electrons to form C4- because it would be difficult for the nucleus with 6 protons to hold on to 10 electrons. It cannot lose 4 electrons to form C4+ because it requires a very large amount of energy to remove four electrons.

teacherNote: You correctly identified that carbon has 4 valence electrons and shares them. However, you must explain the underlying scientific reasons why it cannot gain (nucleus with 6 protons cannot hold 10 electrons) or lose (requires very high energy) four electrons, and write the answer in formal English.

rubric.point: Mentioning carbon has 4 valence electrons and achieves stability by sharing electrons (covalent bonding) to complete its octet/noble gas configuration
Explaining why it cannot gain 4 electrons (6 protons cannot hold 10 electrons) and why it cannot lose 4 electrons (requires a large amount of energy to remove 4 electrons)
